Script

Marketplaces bring clients, payments and reviews, but they also charge fees and have strong competition. Build a clear profile, with a headline that says what you do and for whom. Write proposals that show you read the brief. Early reviews matter a lot. Now the warnings: never move a conversation off the platform before hiring. Never pay a fee to receive work. Never share your password or verification codes. Only trust payment once the money has cleared.

#2voicevoice-en-standardcommercial_ok: yes

Job

20261107-0244-canva-course-voice-01

Script

Templates and digital products can earn while you sleep, because one design can be sold many times. Build them from your own designs. Read the licence of every element, photo and font before you sell. Canva's own elements cannot be sold on their own. Choose a marketplace that suits your product: Etsy, Creative Market, Gumroad, or your own website. For print-on-demand, check each product's print area and order a sample before you trust the quality.

#3voicevoice-en-standardcommercial_ok: yes

Job

20261107-0245-canva-course-voice-01

Script

Canva is one tool in a larger ecosystem. The skills you learned, such as layout, hierarchy, colour and brand consistency, work in every design tool. Learning a second tool is easier than the first. Adobe Express and Google Slides are simple next steps. Figma is popular for app and website design. Illustrator suits logos and icons. CapCut helps with short videos. Confirm current prices and availability on each tool's website before you recommend it to a client.

#4voicevoice-en-standardcommercial_ok: yes

Job

20261107-0246-canva-course-voice-01

Script

Running a freelance business needs basic structure. Check your local registration rules and open a separate bank account. Every paid job needs an invoice with a sequential number. Use a simple written agreement that covers scope, revisions, timeline, payment, ownership and cancellation. Know the licence for every template, photo and font you use. Set aside a share of every payment for tax, and confirm the amount with a local accountant. This video is general guidance, not legal or tax advice.

#5voicevoice-en-standardcommercial_ok: yes

Job

20261107-0246-canva-course-voice-02

Script

This is your 90-day plan. Weeks one and two set up your account and the editor. Weeks three to six build your practice projects and portfolio. Weeks seven to ten bring profiles, outreach and your first paid job. Weeks eleven and twelve review what worked and plan the next quarter. Consistency matters more than speed. Check off the final list before you apply for work. Every professional designer started with a first poster they would redo today. Make your next one this week.
